newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore Refining Co plans maintenance in Mar '97.
newsitem.headline: Singapore Refining Co plans maintenance in Mar '97.

text.p: The Singapore Refining Co (SRC) is planning to shutdown its 90,000-barrel-per-day (bpd) crude distillation unit (CDU) and associated seconday units from early March 1997, an industry source said on Wednesday.
The source said the maintenance at SRC's CDU No.1 will last for 20 days but the turnaround of the secondary units will take 30 days.
The associated secondary units include an 18-million-standard-cubic-feet-per-day hydrogen plant and a 32,000-bpd visbreaker unit.
The visbreaker's shutdown was also to tie with the start up of a new 19,000-bpd asphalt blowing unit.
An 18,000-bpd hydrogen cracker might also be closed at the same time for catalyst regeneration but this has yet to be finalised.
SRC's 285,000-bpd refinery is co-owned by the Singapore Petroleum Corp (SPC), British Petroleum and Caltex, a joint-venture of U.S. majors Chevron Corp and Texaco Inc.
In early October, SRC's 60,000-bpd CDU had a one-week unscheduled shutdown due to technical problems after the unit had run some crude supplies that did not meet its required specifications.
